tools.name: upload_artifact

tools.name: create_upload_url
tools.description: Create a one-time upload URL for a file too large to send as base64 through upload_artifact. The result has upload_url, expires_at, max_size_bytes (25 MiB), ttl_days and filename. The URL is valid for 15 minutes and needs no API key. A PUT of the file's raw bytes to it, for example with curl --uploa

tools.name: list_artifacts
tools.description: List the files in this workspace, newest first. Each entry has id, filename, mime_type, size_bytes, url, expires_at, secret_flags and created_at. Expired files that are not yet deleted are included. The tool changes nothing.

tools.name: revoke_artifact
tools.description: Revoke a file by its id. Its link stops working at once and the file is deleted. The result is revoked: true, or revoked: false when this workspace has no file with that id. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_upload_url, list_artifacts · Private data: upload_artifact, create_upload_url, list_artifacts, revoke_artifact · Public sink: upload_artifact, create_upload_url.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_upload_url, list_artifacts · Private data: upload_artifact, create_upload_url, list_artifacts, revoke_artifact · Public sink: upload_artifact, create_upload_url

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
